title: Random forest on monocyte cell population data aids early COVID-19 identification
summary: Cellular population data from Beckman Coulter DxH 800 blood analysers were compared in 137 controls, 322 COVID-19 patients and 285 patients negative for SARS-CoV-2. A random forest classifier combining four monocyte parameters was tested prospectively in 222 emergency patients, 86 of whom had COVID-19: 60.5% were correctly identified (sensitivity 60.5%) with 89.7% specificity. False negatives were mainly patients with low inflammation and false positives mainly patients with sepsis, so the authors present it only as a possible first step.
ai_technology: Random forest classifier on four monocyte cell population data parameters

evidence.tested: Prospective series of 222 emergency-unit patients (86 COVID-19) with the already built algorithm: sensitivity 60.5%, specificity 89.7%.
evidence.unknown: Sensitivity is modest and the study dates from the early pandemic; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest combined four monocyte parameters to separate COVID-19 from non-COVID patients.
